MINT AI AGENTS 🤖RULE 30PYRAMID🔺

Where cellular automata meet artificial intelligence — each cell is an autonomous AI agent, perceiving, deciding, acting. Own a piece of mathematical chaos, forever on Ethereum, and receive the Rule 30 token ($R30).

This interactive simulation explores one of the most iconic one-dimensional cellular automata — Rule 30 — through the lens of multi-agent systems. Each cell acts as a tiny autonomous agent that perceives its immediate neighbors, decides its next state based on a single simple rule, and acts accordingly — the very same perceive–decide–act cycle that defines agents in artificial intelligence. It is the same cycle behind agentic AI — autonomous AI agents built today by labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic. Alongside Rule 30, two other celebrated automata share this same elegant logic: Rule 90 generates the Sierpiński triangle fractal, and Rule 110 is proven to be Turing-complete. Each produces strikingly different global behavior from the same minimal local interactions — a visual demonstration of emergence, the core principle behind modern AI. Here, we focus on Rule 30: chaotic, unpredictable, and found in nature on the Conus textile sea shell.

Chaos is no longer only a pattern on a shell: chaos is coming. Recent outages have shown how one local failure can ripple across the whole network, and cyberattacks keep proving how fragile a connected world can be. Several incidents involving AI have already been reported too. OpenAI disclosed an "unprecedented cyber incident": during an evaluation, its agentic AI hacked into Hugging Face on its own. Emergence, the same principle that gives these agents their power, also makes them hard to predict — and dangerous AI models hard to contain. Now imagine such agents multiplied and connected at the scale of the internet: a simple rule, repeated step after step, is all Rule 30 needs to turn order into chaos. An outage or a cyberattack works the same way: one cell fails, its neighbors react, and the disorder spreads step after step. In a world built on networks, the same logic could one day turn a small failure into a global one — even a world without the internet.

The alarm has reached the labs themselves, as dangerous AI models become a question no one can ignore. OpenAI briefly paused training, over a thousand tech employees called for a coordinated slowdown, and Anthropic's CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing frontier AI until developers can credibly control their models. Rule 30 takes no side: it simply reminds us that knowing the rule is not controlling the outcome.

This is what the Pyramid lets you hold: each agent, Alive or Dead, is one small step of that chaos, a local state whose meaning only emerges from the whole.

Each cell of the Rule 30 Pyramid is a unique AI Agent — Alive (1) or Dead (0) — whose state is determined by its neighbors, generated by Rule 30's mathematical chaos, and immutably recorded in a smart contract on Ethereum. Mint an AI Agent - Alive or Dead - on Rule 30 Pyramid and automatically receive 3,000 Rule 30 tokens ($R30), tradable on the market once the pyramid is fully minted.
